notes: Ambiguous: reports evidence that 'on its face' supports the exemption, then urges the SEC to re-evaluate the cost-benefit analysis and says investor losses in the <$2bn group are likely to outweigh savings. No explicit position for or against; coded no_position (asks for more analysis). A reader could code do_not_expand or guarded too_broad.

commenter: Campbell Pryde, President and CEO, XBRL US
notes: Duplicate: text identical to s7202618-968360-3005106.pdf (XBRL US). Opposes an XBRL exemption for small NAFs; silent on attestation. XBRL US (data-standards nonprofit) coded other.

commenter: John L. Thornton, Co-Chair, Hal S. Scott, President, and R. Glenn Hubbard Co-Chair, Committee on Capital Markets Regulation
alternative: Vary the length of the post-IPO on-ramp by company size or other objective measures; limit the attestation exemption to smaller issuers rather than all newly public companies.

quotes.quote: The Committee agrees that the costs of ICFR attestation may be disproportionate for some smaller issuers. However, the Proposal would extend this relief beyond small companies
the SEC should consider whether the exemption should instead be limited to those issuers rather than extended to all newly public companies regardless of size.
The SEC should therefore consider whether the duration of the post-IPO on-ramp should vary based on company size or other objective measures

notes: Independent nonpartisan research organisation (members from finance, business, law, accounting, academia); coded other. Guarded: framed throughout as 'should consider' / 'should further evaluate'. Objection centres on the on-ramp for large IPOs; does not evaluate the $2bn figure. Also raises the reach of scaled disclosure to non-FPI foreign companies (not an FPI parity request).

commenter: Richard W. Torgerson, CFA, Registered Principal, SharePower Responsible Investing

quotes.quote: Lastly, we rely on auditor attestation of internal control over financial reporting (ICFR) to guarantee reliability of disclosures and for fraud protection. Eliminating this requirement would put our investments at risk
We urge you to abstain from finalizing this rule

notes: Group of independent financial advisers serving retail investors; coded investor.

commenter: Jaime Bonham, Sr. Director, Head of Responsible Investing, NEI Investments; Hasina Razafimahefa, Director, RI Operations & Strategy, NEI Investments

quotes.quote: We believe it would be detrimental to investors to lose the auditor attestation of internal controls of financial reporting (ICFR) at issuers classified as NAFs under the proposal.
we believe the benefits of protecting investors and maintaining trust in the capital markets outweigh the compliance costs of conducting auditor attestations.

notes: Canadian asset manager. Letter's opening also refers to the registered offering proposal but comments only on S7-2026-18 matters.

commenter: Ali Weiner, Governance Director, Capital Research and Management Company; Walter R. Burkley, General Counsel, Capital Research and Management Company
alternative: Preserve ICFR attestation at minimum for issuers currently subject to it (elsewhere: for issuers meeting today's $700m LAF definition); keep a time-based on-ramp but require market-significant new registrants above a public float or market-significance threshold to comply sooner, including with ICFR attestation.

quotes.quote: We recommend that the Commission not broadly remove the ICFR auditor attestation requirement for all companies that would be treated as NAFs under the Proposal.
we suggest that the Commission preserve auditor attestation at minimum for issuers that are currently subject to the requirement and would become NAFs under the Proposal.
A more tailored approach that preserves the requirement for issuers subject to today’s LAF definition would better balance cost considerations
We therefore recommend a targeted carve-out for market-significant newly public companies such that disclosure obligations scale with objective measures of market significance

notes: Capital Group asset manager. Position ambiguous between do_not_expand and too_broad: one passage asks to preserve attestation for all issuers currently subject to it (no widening), another for issuers meeting 'today's LAF definition' (which would exempt current AFs), and it supports a five-year time-based on-ramp except for mega-caps. Coded too_broad because it accepts some widening (the on-ramp; possibly the AF band). On-ramp coded rejects_or_questions for the size-based carve-out request.

commenter: Eversheds Sutherland (US) LLP on behalf of Committee of Annuity Insurers
notes: Filed by a law firm on behalf of the Committee of Annuity Insurers (coalition of 33 life insurers); coded business_trade_association by the client. Supports the proposal generally; comments concern Article 8 and SAP financial statements for registered insurance contracts, Regulation S-K and Form N-4; silent on 404(b).

commenter: Daniel J. Dustin CPA, NASBA President and CEO, National Association of State Boards of Accountancy ; Nicola Neilon CPA, NASBA Chair, National Association of State Boards of Accountancy
alternative: Before broad elimination, consider alternative assurance: limited assurance on design and implementation of key controls, risk-based attestation for higher-risk NAFs, audit committee certification of oversight of management's assessment, or PCAOB-like inspection of management's assessment for higher-risk NAFs; risk-based factors alongside public float; faster LAF transition for very large or high-risk new issuers.

quotes.quote: NASBA’s most significant concern is the proposal to exempt substantially more public companies from the auditor attestation requirement under Section 404(b) of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act
NASBA is concerned that eliminating the independent attestation requirement for a significantly larger population of public companies will have several unintended consequences.

requiring limited assurance engagements focused solely on the design and implementation of key controls, or a risk-based attestation requirement for higher-risk Non-Accelerated Filers may warrant further consideration before broadly eliminating the independent auditor’s attestation report.
NASBA recommends the SEC reconsider the proposed seasoning requirement or adopt a more flexible framework that allows exceptionally large or high-risk issuers to transition more quickly

notes: Association of state boards of accountancy (regulators of CPAs); coded audit_profession_body. Dated July 17. Supports modernising thresholds and the two-year test; objection to the attestation exemption is framed in guarded terms ('is concerned', 'may warrant further consideration') and it offers lighter-touch alternatives, implying acceptance of some relief; coded too_broad, guarded. Audit committee certification is offered as a regulatory alternative, not as guidance for companies.

commenter: Aaron Bennett, Chief Investment Officer, University Pension Plan Ontario
alternative: Retain 404(b) for companies currently subject to it or, at minimum, above a much lower threshold than $2 billion; retain an accelerated filer category.

quotes.quote: The SEC should retain Section 404(b) attestation for the scope of companies currently subject to it, or at minimum preserve it for issuers above a much lower threshold than proposed.
The proposed US$2 billion large-accelerated filer threshold, expansion of the non-accelerated filer status, and five-year reporting on ramp for issuers following IPO are too broad

notes: Canadian pension plan. Primary ask is to retain attestation for its current scope (do_not_expand, oppose_any_increase); the fallback 'at minimum ... a much lower threshold' could support too_broad / lower.

commenter: BDO USA, P.C.
alternative: Update public float thresholds with inflation adjustments and calibrate by issuer characteristics (scale, complexity, investor following, reporting risk) rather than float coverage alone; two-year transition period for new registrants instead of a five-year seasoning period.

quotes.quote: we are concerned that extending NAF status to approximately 81% of all registrants (which includes the 26.7% of all registrants that would be newly exempt) would eliminate these benefits for many companies that are sizeable, mature, and widely held.
We support updating the existing public float thresholds to reflect changes in market conditions and would support consideration of inflation adjustments as one means of doing so.
we do not believe that historical comparison, standing alone, provides a sufficient basis for extending relief from those requirements to such a broad segment of the public company population.
We believe the proposed five-year seasoning period before qualifying registrants become subject to LAF requirements is too long.

notes: Guarded: objection framed as 'we are concerned' and calls for 'additional analysis'. view_2bn coded lower on the strength of support for inflation-based updating (about $1.15bn) and the view that $2bn reaches too far; BDO names no figure. Also notes FDIC Part 363 attestation for banks over $5bn in assets.

commenter: Campbell Pryde, President and CEO, XBRL US
notes: Opposes an XBRL exemption for small NAFs and urges caution on reduced disclosure; silent on attestation. An identical copy was filed as s7202618-968919-3005649_0.pdf. XBRL US (data-standards nonprofit) coded other; could be business_trade_association.

commenter: Morgan Simon, Founding Partner & CCO, and Tanay Tatum-Edwards, Director of Shareholder Advocacy, Candide Group

quotes.quote: We urge you to abstain from finalizing this rule

notes: Investment adviser. Urges the SEC not to finalize, but the letter discusses disclosures, say-on-pay and information asymmetry only; it never mentions auditor attestation, 404(b) or internal controls, so coded silent (a near-identical template letter from SharePower does include an attestation paragraph).

commenter: Paul F. Washington, President and Chief Executive Officer, Society for Corporate Governance
alternative: Keep $2bn float threshold but consider a supplemental revenue test (e.g. $1.235bn, as a backstop) and a mechanism to recalibrate thresholds; sliding-scale shorter on-ramp (e.g. 24-36 months) for new registrants with float well above $2bn.

quotes.quote: The Society supports extending the scaled disclosure and other accommodations currently available to SRCs and EGCs, including relief from the ICFR auditor attestation requirement under Section 404(b) of SOX, to all NAFs.
The Society supports raising the LAF public float threshold to $2 billion.
we encourage the Commission to consider whether a revenue threshold should be introduced as well (including perhaps, as a backstop if the public float measure is met for two years).

the Society recommends the Commission consider a slide-scale determination for determining LAF status where companies with public float significantly larger than $2 billion have an on-ramp that is shorter than five years
The Society therefore urges the Commission to provide targeted, temporary relief in the form of a grace period or moratorium on filer status changes while this rulemaking is pending.

notes: Professional association of corporate secretaries and governance professionals; coded business_trade_association. The file is very long because it attaches the Society's earlier letters (Reg S-K, executive compensation, semiannual reporting) as appendices; those mention Reg S-K Item 404(b) (related persons), not SOX 404(b). The interim-relief request includes a condition that relying registrants disclose that reliance and their otherwise-applicable filer status; not coded asks_disclosure because it is not a request to disclose whether an attestation was obtained.

commenter: Joshua Stein, Vice President, Accounting & Financial Management, American Bankers Association
alternative: Automatically index the LAF public float threshold for inflation.

quotes.quote: Eliminating the auditor attestation requirement for internal control over financial reporting non-large accelerated filers would be especially meaningful for SEC Issuer community banks
ABA also recommends that the Commission automatically adjust the large accelerated filer public float threshold for inflation.
ABA therefore recommends that the Commission consider whether additional guardrails or a more tailored approach would better balance capital formation objectives with investor protection

notes: Supports the attestation relief; does not separately endorse or evaluate the $2bn figure (a footnote gives its effect on bank issuers), so addresses_2bn_figure left false. Questions the five-year seasoning applied 'without regard to size, complexity, or risk profile'.

commenter: Ernst & Young LLP
alternative: Set the LAF threshold using factors beyond float coverage (trading volume, institutional ownership, market cap, as in 2005); reconsider the 60-month seasoning for large IPOs and rely on the two-consecutive-year test instead.

quotes.quote: we continue to believe the audit of internal control over financial reporting (ICFR) benefits the capital markets by reinforcing management’s ICFR responsibilities and promoting discipline, accountability and transparency in financial reporting.
We recommend that the SEC consider factors beyond the extent of public float coverage when evaluating the appropriateness of the proposed public float threshold
We believe the proposed seasoning requirement may be unnecessary.

We recommend that the SEC reconsider whether this requirement would be appropriate particularly for large-scale companies that are already well-established when they first access public capital markets through an IPO.

We also recommend that the SEC consider whether investors would benefit from disclosure of any filer status changes at the time of registrants’ initial reassessments conducted after adoption of the final rules.

notes: Ambiguous position: says it supports reducing compliance burden 'while maintaining important investor protections', stresses ICFR audit benefits (especially for smaller companies), and questions the threshold basis and the on-ramp in guarded language ('consider', 'may be'). Coded too_broad, guarded; could be read as no_position. addresses_2bn_figure true because it questions how the $2bn figure was set, but it states no direction, so view_2bn left null. Recommends disclosure of filer-status changes at transition; not coded asks_disclosure because it is not disclosure of whether an attestation was obtained, but flag for the third read.

commenter: Eleanor Bloxham, CEO, The Value Alliance and Corporate Governance Alliance

quotes.quote: While the relative efficacy of auditors may be in dispute, the need for accurate, timely financial reports is not.
Do the reforms represent a step in the right direction at this time? No, not at this time.

notes: Governance advisory firm CEO. Opposes the proposal overall, mainly on executive compensation disclosure and governance; mentions auditors and internal controls only in passing ('relative efficacy of auditors may be in dispute'; 'diminished internal controls') without discussing 404(b) or the attestation exemption. Coded silent under the conservative rule; a looser reading would code do_not_expand.

commenter: Joseph P. Corcoran, Managing Director and Associate General Counsel, SIFMA

quotes.quote: SIFMA is submitting this letter in response to the Filer Status Proposal by its July 20 comment letter due date to let the Commission know of SIFMA’s intention to submit a single letter with comments on both proposals.

notes: Placeholder/notice letter: SIFMA says it will file a single substantive letter on S7-2026-17 and S7-2026-18 by July 27, which it did (s7202618-977120-3054308). Linked to that letter as the same filer; the substantive July 27 letter carries SIFMA's codes. A reader might treat this as a memorandum rather than a comment.
